skills.name: Speaking preparation: explaining an effective study plan

note.text: A useful explanation identifies a particular difficulty and links an action to it. Describing a study plan is different from promising instant success for everyone. An example helps an audience understand the proposed action; acknowledging a constraint makes the plan clearer. This lesson prepares written speaking notes. A teacher or partner should later listen, ask a follow-up question and assess clarity, pronunciation and interaction separately.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to prepare a study explanation with a reason, example and realistic adjustment. Builds on: word functions and earlier study routines. Leads to: listening preparation and purposeful essay planning.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model extract: I recognise a definition while looking at it but sometimes cannot explain it with the page closed. My plan is to recall an idea, check the attempt and correct a gap. For example, I can explain a word to a partner before comparing my explanation with the lesson.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the audience, purpose and required content. Plan the order, draft in your own words and check each feature against the model. Explain why an edit improves the answer.

paper_task.prompt: Prepare notes explaining a study difficulty, an action, an example and an adjustment. Rehearse with a partner if possible; this screen assesses written preparation only.
model: I recognise a definition while looking at it but sometimes cannot explain it with the page closed. My plan is to recall an idea, check the attempt and correct a gap. For example, I can explain a word to a partner before comparing my explanation with the lesson.

I will begin after my household tasks. If the available time changes, I will shorten the activity rather than claim I completed it. My partner can ask what supports my explanation. This is a plan to try and review, not a guarantee of a particular examination result.
checklist: Specific difficulty: the particular problem to address.
Reasoned action: a proposed step linked to the difficulty.
Illustrating example: a concrete case clarifying an explanation.
Practical adjustment: a change recognising a constraint.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
